pharm: mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin) inhibitor and rapamycin derivative; inhibits the mTOR serine-threonine kinase signaling pathway, with antiproliferative and immunosuppressive effects.
quick: Take at the same time each day, consistently with or without food
Can cause fetal harm; effective contraception required
Avoid breastfeeding during and for 2 weeks after the last dose
No specific dose adjustment; monitor renal function (renal failure reported)
Reduce dose: 7.5 mg (Child-Pugh A), 5 mg (B), 2.5 mg (C)
Infection, pneumonitis, glucose/lipids, renal function, CBC
summary: Everolimus is an oral kinase (mTOR) inhibitor with potent IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE properties. In oncology it is indicated for HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (with exemestane), progressive neuroendocrine tumors (PNET and GI/lung NET), advanced renal cell carcinoma after sunitinib or sorafenib, and TSC-associated renal angiomyolipoma, SEGA, and partial-onset seizures. Because it is immunosuppressive, everolimus PREDISPOSES PATIENTS TO SERIOUS, sometimes FATAL, INFECTIONS (bacterial, fungal, viral, protozoal, including opportunistic and hepatitis B reactivation) and increases the RISK OF MALIGNANCY-related immune compromise; it also causes non-infectious PNEUMONITIS (a class effect), stomatitis, metabolic disturbances, myelosuppression, and renal failure. The usual oncology dose is 10 mg once daily, with dose reductions for hepatic impairment and CYP3A4/P-gp interactions.
indications: Postmenopausal women with advanced HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, in combination with exemestane, after failure of letrozole or anastrozole
Adults with progressive neuroendocrine tumors of pancreatic origin (PNET), unresectable/locally advanced/metastatic
Adults with progressive, well-differentiated non-functional NET of GI or lung origin, unresectable/locally advanced/metastatic (not for functional carcinoid tumors)
Adults with advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) after failure of sunitinib or sorafenib
Adults with TSC-associated renal angiomyolipoma not requiring immediate surgery
Adult and pediatric patients aged 1 year and older with TSC-associated SEGA requiring intervention but not curatively resectable (tablets and oral suspension)
Adjunctive treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older with TSC-associated partial-onset seizures (oral suspension)

dosage.t: Once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Given with exemestane 25 mg once daily
Not indicated for functional carcinoid tumors
After failure of sunitinib or sorafenib
Titrate to whole-blood trough 5-15 ng/mL; max increment per titration 5 mg

dosage.d: Mild (Child-Pugh A): 7.5 mg/day; Moderate (B): 5 mg/day; Severe (C): 2.5 mg/day
dosage.n: Reduce further if not tolerated (A to 5 mg, B to 2.5 mg); severe only if benefit outweighs risk, do not exceed 2.5 mg

dosage.c: With P-gp and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor
dosage.d: Reduce dose to 2.5 mg once daily (may increase to 5 mg if tolerated)
dosage.n: Resume prior dose 3 days after inhibitor stopped; avoid strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors and grapefruit

dosage.c: With P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducer
dosage.d: Double the daily dose using increments of 5 mg or less
dosage.n: Resume prior dose 5 days after inducer stopped; avoid St. John's Wort

admin: Administer at the same time each day, consistently either with or without food
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not break or crush
Do not combine everolimus tablets and tablets for oral suspension to reach the total dose; select the dosage form by indication
Initiate dexamethasone alcohol-free mouthwash when starting treatment to reduce stomatitis incidence and severity
For oral suspension, prepare in water only, administer immediately, and discard if not given within 60 minutes; wear gloves when preparing for another person
Avoid live vaccines and close contact with recent live-vaccine recipients during treatment
moa: Everolimus is a rapamycin derivative that inhibits mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin), a serine-threonine kinase downstream of the PI3K/AKT pathway. By binding FKBP-12 to form a complex that inhibits mTOR kinase activity, it reduces cell proliferation, angiogenesis, and glucose uptake, producing antitumor effects, and exerts immunosuppressive activity characteristic of the rapamycin class.

absolute: Clinically significant hypersensitivity to everolimus or other rapamycin derivatives
relative: Active or chronic serious infection (immunosuppression worsens infection risk)
Recent or planned major surgery (impaired wound healing)
Severe hepatic impairment (reduce dose; use only if benefit outweighs risk)
monitor: Signs and symptoms of infection (bacterial, fungal, viral, opportunistic; HBV reactivation)

preg: Based on animal studies and its mechanism of action, everolimus can cause fetal harm; embryo-fetal toxicities occurred in rats at maternal exposures lower than the human exposure at 10 mg once daily. Advise pregnant women of the risk. Females of reproductive potential should avoid pregnancy and use effective contraception during treatment and for 8 weeks after the last dose; males with female partners of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 2 weeks after the final dose.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is provided for renal impairment, but renal failure (including acute, sometimes fatal), elevated serum creatinine, and proteinuria have occurred. Monitor renal function before starting and annually thereafter, and at least every 6 months in patients with additional risk factors.
hepatic: Dose reduction is required for hepatic impairment (Breast/NET/RCC/angiomyolipoma): mild (Child-Pugh A) 7.5 mg once daily, moderate (B) 5 mg once daily, severe (C) 2.5 mg once daily only if benefit outweighs risk. For TSC-associated SEGA/seizures with severe impairment, start 2.5 mg/m2 once daily and titrate to trough concentration.

major: P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir): avoid concomitant use
P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's Wort): avoid; if unavoidable, increase everolimus dose
ACE inhibitors: increased risk of angioedema; avoid concomitant use
Live vaccines: avoid due to risk of infection and reduced immune response
moderate: P-gp and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., erythromycin, fluconazole, diltiazem, verapamil): reduce everolimus dose
Other immunosuppressants/corticosteroids: additive immunosuppression; give PJP prophylaxis when used together
interactions.food: Take consistently with or without food; avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice (CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition increases exposure).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol-, hydrogen peroxide-, iodine-, or thyme-containing mouthwash products, which can worsen stomatitis.
interactions.diagnostics: For SEGA and TSC-associated seizures, monitor whole-blood trough concentrations and titrate to 5-15 ng/mL; expect changes in glucose, lipids, and hematologic parameters.

serious: Non-infectious pneumonitis (class effect, up to 19%; fatal cases reported)
Serious and opportunistic infections (sepsis, septic shock, invasive fungal, HBV reactivation; can be fatal)

monitoring: Signs and symptoms of infection, including opportunistic infections and HBV reactivation
Fasting serum glucose and lipid profile before starting and at least annually
Renal function and proteinuria before starting and periodically
CBC before starting, every 6 months in the first year, then annually
counsel: Report promptly any fever, cough, shortness of breath, or other signs of infection or new/worsening breathing problems
Use the prescribed alcohol-free dexamethasone mouthwash to prevent mouth sores; avoid alcohol/peroxide/iodine mouthwashes
Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and St. John's Wort; tell your provider about all medications
Do not receive live vaccines and avoid close contact with people who recently received them
Use effective contraception during treatment (females for 8 weeks, males for 4 weeks after the last dose) and do not breastfeed during and for 2 weeks after treatment
Tell your surgeon you take everolimus, as it must be paused around surgery for wound healing
pk: Antiproliferative effect develops over the treatment course; trough monitoring used for SEGA/seizures
Peak whole-blood concentrations ~1-2 hours after oral dosing
Store per product labeling at controlled room temperature; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Immunosuppressive mTOR inhibitor: serious and opportunistic infections (including fatal sepsis and HBV reactivation) are a key risk
Non-infectious pneumonitis is a rapamycin class effect (up to 19%); evaluate new respiratory symptoms and consider PJP
Prophylactic dexamethasone alcohol-free mouthwash markedly reduces stomatitis (the most common adverse reaction)
Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors raise exposure (avoid) and strong inducers lower it (increase dose); avoid grapefruit and St. John's Wort
Reduce dose in hepatic impairment; monitor glucose, lipids, CBC, and renal function
missed: If a dose is missed, it may be taken up to 6 hours after the usual time; after more than 6 hours, skip that day's dose and resume at the usual time the next day. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited; reported acute single doses up to 70 mg were tolerated with acceptable tolerability. There is no specific antidote; in case of overdose, institute general supportive measures and monitor for adverse reactions including infection, metabolic, and hematologic effects.
